page: OVHcloud d2-8 is a Discovery family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel x86_64 cores based on the Haswell architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity is defined by a 0 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations place the d2-8 in the lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 917.98 falls in the bottom 10%, while the multi-core score of 3730.94 sits in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show 35.67 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 23.03 GB/sec for large-block write operations, both categorized in the bottom 25%. Cryptographic and physics processing are also limited, with Passmark encryption and physics scores landing in the bottom 10%.

Given the shared CPU allocation and older Intel Haswell architecture, this instance presents a clear tradeoff between raw compute power and resource density. It offers a highly cost-efficient entry point for non-production environments where high-performance guarantees are unnecessary. The server is best suited for lightweight workloads such as development environments, basic web serving, small-scale Redis caching, and general-purpose testing.
